name: The Mask

tenures.role: wrestler — UCW World Champion and UCW North American Champion
tenures.source: the character's own career ledger, carried in his signature on the board's own member profile — held in the workshop and not served, this wing's member profiles being withheld whole
tenures.note: Named in-fiction as Stanley Ipkiss throughout his own PWE debut feud. The fed's own text shortens him to “Mask”; the aka is not carried on this row because it auto-linked into unrelated mask-gimmick prose in ACW and MWE.

tenures.role: wrestler — carried the UCW North American Championship into PWE and unified it with the IPW Impact Title
tenures.source: the character's own career ledger, carried in his signature on the board's own member profile — held in the workshop and not served, this wing's member profiles being withheld whole; and PWE's own Deadly Game results of 27 November 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/front-page-news-2005-12-05.html), which records him surviving the Deadly Game match for Team UCW

tenures.role: wrestler — beaten for the TPG Pride Title in the 2007 Showcase
tenures.source: the fed's own “#1 IN Cont's Match” roleplay thread of 10 December 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/1-in-cont-s-match-2005-12-10.html); and the board's own last capture, 27 May 2007 (held in the workshop, not served)
tenures.note: Michael Duncan's own TPG roleplay names him twice as a friend of the promotion's who sent the scout Shawn Berrymoore "to see the talent down here, check out who might be moving up", and confirms the identity in the fed's own words when the scout answers "How do you put up with a guy like The Mask?" with "Stanley? Hehe…". The board's own results panel on its last surviving capture then carries "TPG Showcase: Pride Title: Montel Vontavious Porter © d. The Mask" among the results of PWE's Trials 'N' Tribulations 2007 — his one recorded TPG match, and a loss.

caption: Won Ultimate Championship Wrestling's North American Title in July 2005 and its World Title three weeks later, then carried both onto PWE when the company closed and spent his first promo there explaining, to a demon who had never heard of it, what UCW had been; the last the record sees of him is a TPG Pride Title Showcase in May 2007, which he lost.

name: Michael Hopkins

tenures.source: PWE's own Underground Network of 10 October 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/underground-network-oct-10-milw-wi-2005-10-09.html)

tenures.role: wrestler — introduced on PWE Underground as UCW World Champion
tenures.source: PWE's own Underground Network of 10 October 2005, where Lennex introduces him and The Mask, and the pair threaten Chaos on-camera (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/underground-network-oct-10-milw-wi-2005-10-09.html)
Named as a holder in the fed's own title histories: Pure Championship entry 1.

caption: Introduced on PWE Underground as the UCW World Champion by the man who had just bought the company, and stood beside The Mask while the two of them told the audience what Ultimate Championship Wrestling had been.

name: Trent Hawk

tenures.source: the fed's own invasion promo, delivered on PWE Underground in October 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/mortis-v-the-mask-2005-10-10.html)
tenures.note: The Mask's own promo places their unification match — an Elimination Chamber for his World Title and Hawk's Heavyweight Title — as the last thing UCW announced before it closed.

tenures.source: the fed's own A Belated ‘Sacrifice’, where Headmaster Al takes the belt off him — “This isn't the UCW. This is the Foundation of Brutality. No UCW titles allowed” (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/a-belated-sacrifice-2005-08-17.html) — and PWE's own Deadly Game results of 27 November 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/front-page-news-2005-12-05.html)
tenures.note: The Foundation of Brutality hour of 18 August 2005 carries his match and its result: beaten by Jeremiah Jacobs by pinfall, the announcer calling him “Trent Hawk of the defunct UCW”, after which he superkicked the referee (/promotions/pwe-inc/the wing's own served documents. The match is not structured because that wing's show rows carry no appearances or matches at all.

tenures.source: the fed's own A Belated ‘Sacrifice’, Part One of 17 August 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/a-belated-sacrifice-2005-08-17.html)
tenures.note: He arrived at The Pyramid in a white limo and a white fur coat with the UCW championship under it, and Headmaster Al confiscated it at the door: “The one that said, ‘This isn't the UCW. This is the Foundation of Brutality. No UCW titles allowed’.” He left it with his valet in the limo and went in anyway (the fed's own A Belated ‘Sacrifice’, Part One of 17 August 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/a-belated-sacrifice-2005-08-17.html)). The following night he attacked Jeremiah Jacobs before the bell, put him through the steel steps, missed the superkick, and lost to Out of the Dark — then superkicked the referee for telling him so (the fed's own A belated ‘Sacrifice,’ part deux of 18 August 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/a-belated-sacrifice-part-deux-2005-08-18.html)).

tenures.source: Named as a holder in the fed's own title histories: IPW Championship entry 2, Tag Team Championship entry 2.

caption: Arrived at a Foundation of Brutality show in a white fur coat with the UCW championship under it and had it confiscated at the door; a fortnight later he pinned Lance Storm to win the Deadly Game match for Team UCW at Madison Square Garden.

identity.note: The same ring name on MWA's April 2006 tag card; nothing on either wing's pages ties that record to this one, so the rows stay apart pending a verdict.
